correctness.rationale: Endpoint-forced parity factorization is exact for even and odd path lengths including n=3, with independent signs on all free chain coordinates. The identity between constrained binary chains and signed path independent-set polynomials is algebraic, not heuristic. Fibonacci parity and two explicit 6-periodic signings yield the complete zero/nonzero and sharp gap results for all chain lengths, and multiplication yields the 3-periodic path classification, gap 4, Fibonacci counts and precise Hilbert norms. The packaged Python 3 verifier ran 197234 integer checks against independently implemented full mask enumeration, fast Walsh transforms, direct signed sums and recurrence; finite checks supplement rather than establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The natural object is the complete family of all total dominating sets of labelled paths. The exact spectral rank criterion determines whether a complete signed-incidence observation map is recoverable; the sharp smallest nonzero magnitude determines optimal Hilbert inverse/pseudoinverse stability, uniformly for every size. The two-chain endpoint geometry explains why the exceptional gap is four rather than the single-factor two, yielding a motivated complete infinite-family classification rather than a bare normalization/parity test.
